selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search no longer anchors on segment boundary

evidence.why: The removed `_namespace_prefix_condition` required a `.` separator after the prefix; the new code does `store.prefix LIKE '<prefix>%'` unanchored, so a search scoped to namespace `("foo",)` now also returns items under the sibling namespace `("foobar",)`, `("foo2",)`, etc., crossing tenant/namespace isolation boundaries.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix LIKE unescaped and unanchored

evidence.why: The removed regex-based `_namespace_match_pattern` enforced whole-segment matches (e.g. suffix `alice` would not match `malice`); the new `prefix LIKE '<path>%'` / `LIKE '%<path>'` has no segment anchoring and no escaping of `%`/`_`, so labels containing those characters act as wildcards and prefixes/suffixes match across segment boundaries (e.g. suffix path `alice` now matches namespace ending in `malice`, and a label `user_1` matches `userX1`), leaking namespaces/items that should be isolated.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite namespace prefix search no longer anchors on segment boundary

evidence.why: Replaces the GLOB `(= OR GLOB '<escaped-prefix>.*')` condition with an unescaped, unanchored `prefix LIKE '<prefix>%'`, so a prefix search for `("foo",)` also matches `("foobar",)` and labels containing `%`/`_` are interpreted as wildcards instead of literal characters, crossing namespace isolation boundaries.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite search() namespace_prefix condition unescaped and unanchored

evidence.why: `base_query` now builds `WHERE prefix LIKE ?` with `f"{_namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix)}%"` and no escaping/segment anchoring, so `search(("foo",))` also returns items under `("foobar",)` and labels containing LIKE metacharacters change matching semantics.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix matching loses segment-boundary + case-sensitivity guarantees

evidence.why: Replaces the case-sensitive, segment-anchored GLOB/regex matching (`_namespace_prefix_condition`/`_namespace_match_pattern`/`NS_MATCH_FUNCTION`) with SQLite `LIKE`, which is ASCII case-insensitive and unanchored, so a prefix `foo` matches `Foo`/`foobar` and a suffix `alice` matches `malice`, and `*`-wildcard handling now silently turns any label into an unescaped `%` LIKE wildcard rather than matching exactly one segment.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade requests with a body are no longer drained, enabling request smuggling

evidence.why: cb_on_headers_complete now returns 2 (pause, treat rest as upgrade tail) as soon as an Upgrade header is present, instead of deferring the switch until the body is fully consumed as the old _pending_upgrade logic did. If the application handler declines the upgrade (never actually switches protocol), the request body bytes are handed back as opaque 'tail' data rather than parsed, so those bytes can be reinterpreted as the start of the next pipelined HTTP request -- exactly the scenario the removed test_declined_websocket_upgrade_reads_body and the deleted 13016.bugfix.rst entry guarded against.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Python parser marks connection upgraded before body is read, skipping payload for declined upgrades

evidence.why: self._upgraded is now set immediately from msg.upgrade/_is_supported_upgrade and used to suppress payload creation (`and not self._upgraded`), removing the previous 'pending upgrade' deferral that only flips _upgraded after the body is fully read; a request with Connection: Upgrade plus a body whose upgrade is ultimately declined by the handler will have its body left unconsumed by the parser and treated as protocol tail/next-request data.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.
